features.headline: MLB free agency tracker: 2026-27 offseason trades, moves
features.desc: We've got you covered on all the major MLB hot stove signings and trades.
body: The 2026-27 MLB hot stove was lit just days after the Milwaukee Brewers hoisted the franchise's first World Series championship trophy.
Which teams will go big to contend for the 2027 World Series title? And who will make the trades and signings that have everyone buzzing?
Below is a running list of notable transactions and updates from throughout the MLB offseason.
Right-hander Freddy Peralta and the Baltimore Orioles are in agreement on a five-year, $125 million contract, sources tell ESPN.
Left-hander Kris Bubic and the Cleveland Guardians are in agreement on a one-year, $17.5 million contract, sources tell ESPN.
The Chicago Cubs have reached an agreement with Japanese Central League MVP Teruaki Sato on a six-year, $120 million contract, sources tell ESPN.
Infielder Ha-Seong Kim and the Detroit Tigers are in agreement on a one-year, $5 million contract, sources tell ESPN.
The Chicago Cubs have agreed to a five-year, $120 million contract with free agent pitcher Trevor Rogers, sources familiar with the situation told ESPN.
The New York Mets continued their spending spree by coming to terms on a one-year deal with first baseman Paul Goldschmidt, a source told ESPN.
Left-handed reliever Brent Suter and the New York Yankees are in agreement on a one-year, $4 million contract with a club option for 2028, sources tell ESPN.
The Kansas City Royals signed left-hander Caleb Thielbar to a one-year, $3.25 million contract, sources told ESPN.
Tarik Skubal and the New York Mets are in agreement on a nine-year, $450 million contract, sources tell ESPN.

features.headline: One trade ESPN experts would make before MLB lockout
features.desc: An MLB lockout is looming. Our experts suggest some last-minute deals.
body: Say it with us: Major League Baseball is about to shut down.
But wait! Before the lockout begins — which, if you haven't heard, is expected to happen Tuesday, Dec. 1, at 11:59 p.m. ET — there remains a lot of business to get done.
Although all the offseason free agent signings and trades won't be made in the next week, a lot of them will (and already have been).

While we wait for a potential flurry of moves, we asked our MLB experts to share one deal — specifically, a trade — they'd love to see made before the league goes dark. Here is how they responded, starting with a pair of swaps involving a Boston outfielder.
A year ago, such a paltry return would have been unthinkable for Duran, who generated 13.9 bWAR in 2024-25 thanks to a robust batting line (124 OPS+) and outstanding defensive metrics (32 DRS).
But his value cratered in 2026, as he mustered 0.4 bWAR and a 76 OPS+, rendering him a non-tender candidate with a projected $11 million arbitration salary looming.
Corbin Carroll anchors an Arizona outfield with reliably little else, and the contours of Chase Field would amplify Duran's propensity for doubles and triples. — Paul Hembekides
Phillies executive Dave Dombrowski led the Red Sox when the organization drafted Duran in 2018, but he was long gone by the time Duran became an All-Star in 2024.
Duran's 2026 campaign was obviously a struggle, and the Red Sox boast depth among their corner outfielders. The Phillies certainly do not.

With no immediate path to the rotation for 2025 first-round pick Wood, and no certainty that he remains on track for an eventual rotation spot, it would hardly be surprising to see the aggressive Dombrowski move another top prospect for immediate aid.

features.headline: 2026-27 MLB free agency, trade grades: Offseason analysis
features.desc: We've got you covered with grades and analysis on every winter signing and big offseason trade.
body: The 2026-27 MLB offseason is officially here, and we have you covered with grades and analysis for every major signing and trade as this winter — which is expected to include a labor stoppage — unfolds.
Whether it's a franchise-changing free agent signing or an unexpected blockbuster trade, we'll weigh in with what it all means for next season and beyond.

ESPN MLB experts Bradford Doolittle and David Schoenfield will evaluate each move as it happens, so follow along here, as this story will continue to be updated. Check back in for all the most recent analysis.
Skubal to NYM | Peralta to BAL Sato to CHC | Gray to MIN | Bauers to BOS

The Cleveland Guardians are getting spendy! The $17.5 million deal they struck with Kris Bubic is a franchise record for a one-year free agent contract and, unofficially, ties the club record for any one-year contract.
Francisco Lindor inked an arbitration-fueled deal for the same amount in 2020 that included incentives he did not reach. So, in Cleveland, Bubic equals Lindor.
In all seriousness, I'm a big Bubic guy who once touted him as a Cy Young contender, and I did so before his 2025 breakout season.
He was on track to earn some Cy Young votes that year, too, before his season was clipped due to one of a string of injuries with which he's had to deal with over the past few seasons.
Hence the one-year contract, one that Bubic has to be looking at as a make-good opportunity with a team that has a proven track record with hurlers.
It's a win-win for both sides. Bubic gets a handsome one-year payout and, with a healthy platform season, would be in line to earn much more next year.

features.headline: Drew Stevens goes viral with hilarious postgame presser after winning kick
features.desc: Stevens' explanation for how he calms himself down in tense moments took the internet by storm.
body: LANDOVER, Md. — The Washington Commanders got the clutch Drew Stevens. The news conference got the authentic one. Both ended up winning the night. There's a reason one media member asked at the end of Stevens' presser early Tuesday morning: "Can he come in every week?"

After kicking five field goals, including the game-winning 27-yarder with no time remaining to beat the Cincinnati Bengals 22-20, Stevens recalled his thoughts in an entertaining manner as he headed out for the attempt.
He sat at a table in the news conference, a place reserved for coaches, quarterbacks and stars of the game. It was Stevens' first time sitting in that chair.
A lot of it was focused on a phrase he often tells himself — which helps explain why he beat out Jake Moody to make the Commanders' roster as an undrafted free agent this summer.
Stevens was asked how he calms himself in those tense moments, especially when all he needed to do was hit a chip-shot, 26-yard field goal.

"I mean, authentic Drew Stevens, you really want to know what I tell myself?" he said. "I sit there and I'm like, 'OK, I'm going to have kids. Am I going to tell my kids that their dad was a little...
you know.' Or am I going to tell my kids, 'Yeah, your dad walked out there and he drilled it and he was ready for it?' That's what I'm telling them. Because that's how it happened."

His gestures added to the moment: pointing his finger, cocking his head, lowering his voice. His answer and movements were greeted with chuckles. That prompted him to nod his head and simply say, "yeah" and laugh a little himself as he scanned the media gathering.

features.headline: What Todd Monken's six keys reveal about the Browns' offense
features.desc: Let's look at the six pillars the first-year head coach stands by and how they're helping (or hurting) Cleveland's offense.
body: BEREA, Ohio — Before Cleveland Browns players left the team's facility for their bye last week, quarterback Deshaun Watson dismissed the idea of entertaining playoff talk this early.
"Coach [Todd Monken] don't even mention it... We're not getting ahead of ourselves. Most of the guys are thinking about [Grand Theft Auto], for real," Watson said.
The Browns, though, return from their bye, and reaching the playoffs for the first time since 2023 is an increasingly attainable and likely goal.

Cleveland moved up one spot to the AFC's sixth seed after the Pittsburgh Steelers' loss to the Philadelphia Eagles. Losses by the Baltimore Ravens and Las Vegas Raiders, the latter of whom the Browns will host on "Sunday Night Football"
in Week 12 (8:20 p.m. ET, NBC), only helped boost Cleveland's playoff odds, which sit at 57.5%, according to ESPN Analytics.
Cleveland (6-4) has already exceeded last year's win total and is ahead of schedule with the second-youngest team in the NFL.
Despite losing reigning Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett and coordinator Jim Schwartz, Cleveland's defense hasn't taken a step back with first-year coordinator Mike Rutenberg.

It's the Browns offense, though, which will likely determine the team's fate. Cleveland has shown growth after scoring the fewest points in the NFL over the previous two seasons, but the unit still ranks 26th in scoring this season (18.8 PPG).
Slow starts have plagued the Browns, who are the only team in the league that has not scored on its opening drive.

features.headline: NBA Rookie Rankings: 10 standouts in a star-studded class
features.desc: Our first edition of rookie rankings features 10 players standing out early from a strong 2026 draft class.
body: It's hard to succeed as a rookie in the NBA — even as a high pick in one of the most highly touted drafts in recent memory.

Consider that, through Sunday's games, the top 10 picks from June's draft are shooting a combined 41% from the field and 32% from 3-point range so far, with only Kingston Flemings checking in above 45% and 35%, respectively.
That inefficiency doesn't make this rookie class any less exciting. In fact, this class is both star-studded at the top and very deep in the middle.
Our first rookie rankings of the season will list only 10 players but could very easily extend twice as long with promising prospects and useful contributors.
Note that this is primarily a ranking of the quality of the rookies' play right now, with only a bit of long-term projection factored.

Honorable mentions at this point of the season include: Bennett Stirtz (Oklahoma City); Trevon Brazile (Denver); Ryan Conwell (Miami); Brayden Burries (Milwaukee); Mikel Brown Jr. (Brooklyn); Zuby Ejiofor (Atlanta); and Allen Graves (Toronto).

The good news for Wagler is that he's getting to the free throw line consistently (5.0 attempts per game) and making 35% of his 3-pointers. The bad news is he's also making 35% of his 2s, which is a frighteningly low number that portends greater concerns about his ceiling as an offensive engine.

Still, the 19-year-old has provided steady production off the bench for the Clippers, with double-digit points in 11 of his first 13 games before a slump over the weekend. That consistency is far from a given for most rookies.
